poster_title: Test-Time Preference Optimization: On-the-Fly Alignment via Iterative Textual Feedback
authors: Yafu Li, Xuyang Hu, Xiaoye Qu, Linjie Li, Yu Cheng

content: Large language models (LLMs) may produce unsafe responses if not aligned.
Traditional alignment methods are not swift enough for real-time adaptation.
Need for a method to align LLMs during inference with textual feedback.
Aligning LLMs during inference to match human preferences.
Using interpretable textual feedback for preference optimization.
TPO transforms numerical rewards into textual critiques.
Policy model refines outputs iteratively based on textual critiques.
TPO operates as an online, on-policy learning paradigm.
Evaluated on benchmark datasets: instruction following, preference alignment, safety, mathematics.
Compared unaligned and aligned models, with aligned models optimized at training time.
TPO aligns the policy model with human preferences, improving reward model scores.
Unaligned Llama-3.1-70B-SFT surpasses Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct on most benchmarks.
TPO scales efficiently with search width and depth.
TPO is a practical and lightweight method for test-time preference optimization.
Empirical findings show significant improvement in alignment with human preferences.
